title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 416
paragraphs: Such is the nature of the so-called Table of the Sun as described. So when Cambyses had resolved to send the spies, he at once sent for those of the Ichthyophagoi who understood the Ethiopian tongue to come from the city of Elephantine. While they were going to fetch these men, he gave the order for the fleet to sail against Carthage. But the Phoenicians said they would not do so, for they were bound not to by solemn vows, and they would not be acting piously by making an expedition against their own sons. Since the Phoenicians were unwilling, the rest were rendered unequal to the attempt. Thus the Carthaginians escaped being enslaved by the Persians; for Cambyses did not think it right to use force to compel the Phoenicians, both because they had delivered themselves over to the Persians of their own accord and because the entire naval force depended on the Phoenicians. The men of Cyprus too had delivered themselves over to the Persians and were joining in the expedition against Egypt.
